title: VPC decision sampler and rollback heuristics (PRD draft)
body:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures a proposed PRD for two tightly coupled features for Private Deployments: a decision-sampling subsystem (decision sampler) that reduces audit volume while preserving forensic fidelity, and a set of rollback heuristics/fallbacks that operators and customers can rely on during VPC/network changes. Intention is to design a lightweight, testable first release that is safe for pilot customers and instrumented for later tuning.

Goals:
- Provide a configurable sampling policy so we don't store full change payloads for every VPC operation but can still reconstruct causal chains for incidents.
- Guarantee fast rollback triggers with deterministic safety checks (attestation + evidence) so operator and customer can execute rollbacks automatically or with one-click.
- Offer clear observability/QA hooks: sampled replay artifacts, sampling coverage metrics, SLOs for rollback decision latency, and explainability for decisions made by automated agents.

Non-goals (v1):
- Full cryptographic escrow for all proofs (we'll ship compact attestations in v1 and iterate on escrow APIs).
- Complex ML-based anomaly detection—basic heuristics only.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Decision event: any operator-initiated or customer-initiated VPC change (route updates, firewall rules, peering, NAT changes).
- Sampled evidence bundle (SEB): the compact artifact stored when a decision is sampled. SEB contains meta, diffs, minimal device logs, signed attestations (where present), and pointers to full payloads in customer storage (if customer allows).
- Rollback token: a signed assertion that allows automatically reversing a previous decision when preconditions are met. Tokens can be constrained (time-window, scope, operator).

User stories:
- As a Redwood operator, I want 5–50% sampling of high-frequency rule changes so that my audit store doesn't blow up but I can still investigate incidents with high confidence.
- As a customer network admin, I want the ability to trigger a deterministic rollback for the last N changes in a change window with evidence checks to avoid accidental reversions.
- As an SRE, I want metrics on sampled vs total decisions and a replay API to reconstruct an incident from sampled bundles.

Sampling policy sketch (configurable):
- GlobalDefault: 10% of decisions across the tenant by default.
- RouteChangeBoost: route-table and NAT changes are boosted to 30% by weight.
- OperatorOptIn: individual named operators can opt into 100% capture for a session (useful for on-call debugging).
- HotWindow: if an error rate spike is detected (>=5 controller errors in 1 minute), switch to catch-all sampling for 10 minutes.

SEB minimal schema (human-readable example; v1 stores as compact newline-delimited JSON blob):
- id: sampling-id-20250211-0001
- tenant_id: tenant-123
- timestamp: 2025-02-11T14:03:22Z
- decision_type: ROUTE_TABLE_UPDATE
- operator: elena.ruiz@redwood.ai
- delta_summary: "added route 10.20.0.0/16 -> igw-1; removed route 10.21.0.0/16"
- evidence_refs: ["s3://cust-logs/tenant-123/changelog/2025-02-11/0001.gz"] (if customer consented)
- signed_attest: "k:v:base64sig" (optional)
- replay_hint: "requires full config snapshot at t-5m"

Storage and retention policies:
- SEBs are small (target < 2KB compressed). Retention defaults to 90 days for sampled bundles.
- Index entries (metadata) retained 365 days for audit search.
- Customers can opt into longer retention or export SEBs to their storage.

Rollbacks and safety checks:
- Rollback preconditions (all must pass for auto-rollback):
  1) Evidence match: SEB present or identical delta in the immutable change log (if customer exports archive).
  2) Attestation sanity: operator signature exists or token issued by Redwood operator system.
  3) Dependency check: downstream resources unaffected or compensating actions exist (e.g., route removal doesn't orphan subnets).
  4) Time-window: rollbacks allowed within 72 hours by default unless customer config allows longer.

Rollback modes:
- Auto-rollback: triggered by detection rules (e.g., control-plane error spike) and preconditions satisfied.
- Assisted rollback: UI-guided; operator sees confidence score and required manual approvals to execute.
- One-click customer rollback: for customer-managed networks with delegated rollback permissions.

Decision explainability and logs:
- Every rollback action must contain a compact decision trace: origin decision id(s), preconditions checked, operator who approved, and a human-readable rationale.
- We maintain a small decision graph index mapping decision id -> parent ids to allow traversal. Graph index is stored separately from SEBs.

Observability and SLOs:
- Sampling coverage metric: sampled_decisions / total_decisions per tenant (target initial: 12% ± 3%).
- Rollback latency SLO: 95th percentile decision->rollback initiation <= 30s for auto-rollbacks during an incident.
- Replay fidelity SLO: For sampled incidents, ability to replay and obtain config snapshot that reproduces the change within 5 minutes of orchestration time in 90% of cases.

Operator UX and Console primitives (quick notes):
- Sampling dashboard: per-tenant toggle, histogram of decision types, recent SEB previews (read-only), and export buttons.
- Rollback console: timeline view with decisions, confidence badges, "simulate rollback" button that runs dry-run checks against a target snapshot.
- Explainability panel: natural-language summary + structured checks that were performed.

Pilot plan (4-week pilot w/ 2 customers):
Week 0: baseline data collection (no sampling) and capacity planning.
Week 1: enable 10% sampling for pilot tenants + realtime metrics.
Week 2: enable HotWindow + rollback UI (assisted mode only).
Week 3: enable auto-rollback for one non-critical change type (route removals) with aggressive preconditions; collect postmortems.

Acceptance criteria (v1):
- Sampling reduces audit storage growth by >= 60% for high-change tenants while preserving at least one complete evidence bundle for 95% of incident investigations (measured via simulated incident corpus).
- Rollback flow executes safely in assisted mode for pilot customers with no more than 1 human rollback per 500 automated checks (safety verification).
- Observability: sampling coverage and replay success visible in console; linked artifacts export works.

Open questions / risks:
- Legal/compliance: will SOC2/PCI auditors accept sampled evidence for major incident reconstructions? May need attestation escrow option.
- Customer consent model: how to handle customers who strictly disallow any off-box evidence_refs? Offer local-only SEBs that store envelope metadata but no external refs.
- Replay determinism: cloud provider variability can make post-hoc replay noisy. Need fuzzy-replay mode and a clear "replay confidence" metric.
- Cost modeling: SEB indexing and small-size retention still adds cost—need finance model for per-tenant indexing surcharge or include in Dedicated cap.

Implementation notes (engineering constraints):
- SEBs should be generated as part of the existing change pipeline (before apply) to capture request/intent.
- Use streaming index writer to ensure durability of metadata even when payload storage is deferred.
- Rollback tokens signed with rotating key (KMS/HSM integration) and short TTL by default.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Action: eng (platform) to prototype SEB generation hook in change pipeline. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Action: product to draft tenant-facing consent language and default retention options. Owner: Ravi. ETA: 1 week.
- Action: legal to review sampling approach for audit acceptability. Owner: Elena. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Action: design to mockup rollback console flows and confidence badges. Owner: Liam. ETA: 1 week.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally conservative on auto-rollback; we prefer assisted-first for pilot.
- Look for missing edge cases where sampling could remove critical evidence (e.g., multi-step operator runs that are each sampled separately).

Appendix: quick scenario (narrative)
- Sequence: customer deploys a bulk NAT rule change via Terraform (5k routes). Controller returns partial failure; downstream connectivity intermittently fails. Our HotWindow detects the error spike and switches to full sampling. SEBs captured for the first failing changes contain minimal diffs and a pointer to customer-provided config snapshot. Using SEBs plus graph index, operator identifies the offending change id and triggers an assisted rollback; preconditions validate, and rollback executes within 22s. Post-incident, the replay artifacts (SEB + exported snapshot) were sufficient to root-cause a provider API throttling problem.

-- end of draft --
